title: MR spectroscopy to determine neurotransmitters in healthy people and epilepsy patients, comparing 3 Tesla to 7 Tesla.
summary:
This study investigates how accurately magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) can measure the concentration of the neurotransmitters GABA and glutamate in the brain. For this purpose, two different MRI devices with different magnetic field strengths (3 Tesla and 7 Tesla) are compared. The study will be carried out on both healthy adults and epilepsy patients.
A total of 25 people will take part - 10 epilepsy patients and 15 healthy volunteers aged between 18 and 65. Exclusion criteria are people who have previously undergone brain surgery, are taking medication that influences the release of the neurotransmitters to be analysed, are addicted to drugs or alcohol, are pregnant or breastfeeding or have a mental illness.
Each participant is examined on both MRI scanners on two consecutive days. Three subjects will also receive a second measurement on the same day to check the repeatability of the results. The examinations take place at the Cooperative Brain Imaging Centre (CoBIC) in Frankfurt.
